formalization.objective: minimize elastic strain energy density h (meV/A^3) of Si
constraints: Eg <= 0 eV (metal; CBM at or below VBM), evaluated at HSE06-scissor level (PBE valley energies plus zero-strain HSE corrections; G 0.764, L 0.763, D 0.582 eV). The PBE gap alone is not enough because PBE underestimates the Si gap (0.607 vs 1.189 eV at zero strain).
Target margin Eg <= -0.05 eV at hse_scissor to cover the surrogate error (holdout MAE 0.043 eV)
formalization.subspace: All 6 Green-Lagrange Voigt components free, |strain| <= 0.08 (normal) and 0.06 (shear)
formalization.stability: Born elastic stability not checked (12-unit cost). At h of about 2.5 meV/A^3 the state is well below the ideal-strength regime, but this is not verified.
formalization.level_of_theory: hse_scissor for the search and ranking; PBE DFT with internal relaxation for the data. Full HSE06 verification not run (tool denied).

designer.explanation: Campaign: 20 Latin-hypercube PBE DFT points, then a surrogate fit and optimisation at hse_scissor, then DFT checks of the 4 optimiser candidates. After refitting, a second optimisation with a -0.05 eV margin gave 3 more DFT checks. In total 27 PBE points were used, with 123 of 150 budget units left. Physics: metallisation means the lowest conduction valley (a Delta valley, Dx/Dy/Dz) drops below the VBM. Si's CBM is already a Delta valley (0.607 eV in PBE, 1.189 eV in HSE). Gamma (about 1.4 eV) and L (0.4 to 1.7 eV) stay well above it at the optimum, so they are not involved. Shear-dominated strain, as in this candidate (e12 = -0.049 with e33 = -0.023), splits the Delta valleys and pushes one (Dz here) far down. The cheapest route to a zero gap is therefore to lower a single Delta valley by about 1.19 eV (HSE) with minimal energy. Results at hse_scissor: a candidate at h = 2.31 gave Eg = +0.03 eV, which is not metallic. The chosen candidate at h = 2.558 gave Eg = -0.087 eV (PBE gap -0.669 eV), which satisfies the constraint. Two other candidates at h = 2.64 gave Eg of about -0.107 eV. The true minimum-h metal is probably near h of about 2.4, where Eg crosses zero, but I did not sample it directly. I could not run the full HSE06 check (verify_hse was denied), so Eg = -0.087 eV is a scissor estimate, not a verified HSE06 value.

verifier.stable: Yes. Born stable, minimum stiffness eigenvalue 30.6 GPa.
issues: Fresh PBE DFT reproduces the claim: h = 2.558 meV/A^3, PBE gap -0.669 eV (Dz CBM), hse_scissor gap -0.087 eV. The scissor arithmetic is consistent (-0.669 + 0.582 = -0.087).

Full HSE06 gives Eg = -0.208 eV (Dz valley at -0.208 eV, next lowest Dx at 0.55 eV). The metal constraint holds, and the -0.05 eV margin holds with room to spare. The scissor estimate was conservative by about 0.12 eV.
The team did not check Born stability. I ran it, and the state is stable (min eigenvalue 30.6 GPa).

The metallic character depends on a single valley: Dz is at -0.208 eV in HSE06, while Dx and Dy are still above 0.5 eV. The gap closes through large shear-driven valley splitting, so it is sensitive to the e12 = -0.049 component.

I did not verify that h = 2.558 is the minimum. I only confirmed feasibility, h, and stability at this one point. I did not search for lower-h states or check symmetry-equivalent strains, which would have the same h and gap.
Conventions are consistent: Green-Lagrange, Voigt, tensor shear, fractions. All components are within the stated bounds (|normal| <= 0.08, |shear| <= 0.06).
